citation: Treaty with the Potawatomi, 1815 (Portage des Sioux, 18 July 1815; 7 Stat. 123), in Charles J. Kappler, ed., Indian Affairs: Laws and Treaties, vol. II, Treaties (Washington: Government Printing Office, 1904).
author: the United States commissioners William Clark, Ninian Edwards and Auguste Chouteau, and the chiefs and warriors of the Potawatomi residing on the Illinois River; compiled by Charles J. Kappler
repository: Oklahoma State University Libraries, Tribal Treaties Database (Kappler vol. II transcription)
locator: Article 1 (the forgiving of 'Every injury or act of hostility'); the signatures: Sunawchewome, Neggeneshkek, Chawcawbeme, Bendegakewa, 'Wapewy, or White Hair', Outawa, each 'his x mark'.
rights_note: A United States treaty and a 1904 Government Printing Office compilation; public domain. Read as the OSU transcription.
access_notes: Read 2026-11-08 for T-3508 from the OSU page (fetched that day). The names are as Kappler prints them; the clerks' spellings of Potawatomi names vary from treaty to treaty.
note: THE PEACE OF THE ILLINOIS RIVER POTAWATOMI after the war of 1812. Its signers are men of the bands that gathered at Chicago in August 1812; the treaty does not say any of them was there.
what_it_supplies: the names of six chiefs and warriors of the Illinois River Potawatomi in 1815, one with its English gloss
what_it_does_not_supply: where any signer was in August 1812
